justification: The proof's composition formula and cross-term vanishing are essentially correct, but the pure composition laws are false for non-rational closed points. In (1a) the restriction of p13 to X x {p} x {q} is not an isomorphism onto X x {q}; it is the projection (X x {q}) x_k {p} -> X x {q}, finite of degree [k(p):k], so p13*([X x {p} x {q}]) = deg(p) H_q and hence H_p o H_q = deg(p) H_q, not H_q. The local affine verification over QQ with x2=0 and x3=0 only treats rational points. In (1b) the analogous map {p} x {q} x X -> {p} x X is finite of degree [k(q):k], not an isomorphism, so V_p o V_q = deg(q) V_p, not V_p. Therefore Step 2 is invalid: A o A should be (sum_p a_p deg(p)) A and B o B should be (sum_q b_q deg(q)) B, while the hypotheses only give sum_p a_p = sum_q b_q = 0. The statement is in fact false as written: for X = P^1_R, p rational and q a closed point of degree 2, alpha = H_p - H_q has sum of coefficients 0, is nonzero in CH^1(X x X) (its class is -H), and alpha^2 = -alpha (equivalently H) is nonzero. A correct proof would need to assume all p and q are k-rational, or replace the zero-sum conditions by the degree-weighted conditions sum_p a_p deg(p)=0 and sum_q b_q deg(q)=0 and use the degree-corrected composition laws; with those changes the expansion would give alpha^2=0. The description of CH_1 as a free abelian group on effective divisors modulo rational equivalence is also imprecise, but not the decisive error.
